chunks: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): My companion (wife) has died, and she was compatible for me, and I have thought about getting married. So he said to me: Consider where you are placing yourself, and whom you are associating in your wealth, and making privy to your religion and your secrets. If you must do it, then marry a virgin who is attributed to goodness and to good character.

And know that they (women) are as has been said: 'Indeed! Women were created of various sorts — among them is the beneficial and the loss-maker, and among them is the crescent moon when it shines for its companion, and among them is the darkness. So whoever succeeds with the righteous among them will be fortunate, and whoever is deceived, there is no recourse for him.'

And they are three types: A fertile, affectionate woman who supports her husband against the trials of time for his worldly life and his hereafter, and does not let time work against him; and a barren woman without beauty or good character, who does not assist her husband toward goodness; and a clamorous, intrusive, fault-finding woman who belittles what is much and does not accept what is little.

key_terms.الْغَرَامُ: Literally 'loss/debt/passion' — poetically used for a burdensome wife
key_terms.الْغَنِيمَةُ: Literally 'war-spoils/gain' — poetically used for a wife who is a blessing
key_terms.حُسْنُ الْخُلُقِ: Good character/morals — a central Islamic ethical virtue
key_terms.صَخَّابَةٌ: Clamorous, loud — describing a contentious wife
key_terms.مُوَافِقَةً: Compatible, agreeable — used here for a harmonious marital relationship
key_terms.هَمَّازَةٌ: Fault-finder, backbiter — one who seeks out faults in others
key_terms.وَلَّاجَةٌ: Intrusive, one who frequently enters others' affairs
key_terms.وَلُودٌ وَدُودٌ: Fertile and affectionate — a Prophetic description of an ideal wife

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about choosing the right woman for marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith records a consultation between Ibrahim al-Karkhi and Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about remarriage after the death of his wife. The Imam advises careful deliberation about whom one chooses as a spouse, emphasizing that a wife becomes partner in one's wealth and confidante in one's religious life. He then cites Arabic poetry — well-known in 2nd-century AH literary culture — to illustrate the diversity of women's characters, before offering a practical typology of three female archetypes: the ideal supportive wife, the neutral barren wife, and the destructive quarrelsome wife.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Ahmad Bin Muhammad altogether, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Al Karkhy who said, 
‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘My female companion died and she was compatible for me and I have thought about getting married’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Consider where you are placing yourself and the one you are associating in your wealth, and aspiring to be upon your Religion, and your secrets. So if it was inevitable to do, so (get married to) a virgin who has been linked to goodness, and to good mannerisms.

And know that they (women) are as just as if has been said, ‘Indeed! The women are of various etiquettes – so from them is the beneficial, and the loss maker, and from them is the crescent shining for her companion, and from them is the darkness. So the one who succeeds with a righteous one would be fortunate, and the one who is cheated so it is not for him that he takes revenge.

They are three (types) – A child bearing woman of cordiality and supportive of her husband all the time for his world and his Hereafter, and she does not spend time against him; and a sterile (barren) woman, not with any beauty nor manners, and she does not assist her husband upon goodness; and a vociferous (loud) woman, a fault-finder, belittling the lot, and not accepting the little’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from all ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim al-Karkhiy who has said the following: “I once said to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘My wife who lived in complete harmony with me has died and I want to marry.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Think where you want to place yourself and whom you are making your partner in your assets, inform of your religion and secrets. If you must marry find a virgin who is spoken of with goodness and of good moral discipline.

You must take notice that women are as it is said: ‘Women are of various moral manners; among them are gains and losses. Among them are lawful when she shines for her companion and among them is darkness. Whoever succeeds in finding the righteous among them is a sure fortunate but one who is cheated cannot revenge.

‘They are of three kinds; one kind is a child bearing and loving who helps her husband all the time in the worldly as well as the matters of the hereafter and the world does not work against her. The other kind is woman who is barren without beauty and moral manners and does not help her husband in anything good, she is loud and noisy, roaming around and faultfinding who considers a great deal very little and does not accept things of lesser amount.’”
